title: Grid Systems in Graphic Design: A Visual Communication Manual for Graphic Designers, Typographers and Three Dimensional Designers
authority: Swiss graphic designer (1914-1996), a leading figure of the International Typographic Style; the book is the canonical text on the typographic grid.
caveats: A designer's treatise, not empirical research. Claims about the grid's communicative benefit are untested experimentally. Shaped for print; web use needs translation. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: Designing Programmes
edition: German original Programme entwerfen, 1964; English edition later (4th ed., Lars Müller, 2007)
authority: Swiss designer and co-founder of GGK (1959); author of the Capital magazine grid and a pioneer of systematic, programmatic design.
caveats: Theoretical and polemical; no empirical evidence. Exact grid unit counts quoted from memory should be checked against the book. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: The Vignelli Canon
authority: Massimo Vignelli (1931-2014), co-founder of Unimark, designer of the NYC Subway signage system and American Airlines identity.
caveats: Personal doctrine of a modernist; strong opinions (very few typefaces, strict grids) are not evidence-based and are one school among several. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: The Grid: A Modular System for the Design and Production of Newspapers, Magazines, and Books
authority: Allen Hurlburt (1910-2004), art director of Look magazine and long-time design educator.
caveats: Editorial and print oriented; historical proportion theory sections inherit the golden-ratio enthusiasm later criticized (see Markowsky1992). Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: Making and Breaking the Grid: A Graphic Design Layout Workshop
authority: Designer and educator (Parsons, Pratt); widely used layout text that systematizes grid types and deliberate departures.
caveats: Practice-based, no empirical testing. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: A Practical Guide to Designing for the Web
authority: Mark Boulton, designer and author who adapted print grid theory to the web in his Five Simple Steps essays (2005-2007) and later Designing for the Web.
caveats: Written in the fixed-width era; pixel examples are dated though principles hold. Details of the five steps should be checked. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: Responsive Web Design
authority: Coined the term; essay in the leading professional web design publication, expanded into the 2011 A Book Apart book.
caveats: Later practice shifted toward content-driven breakpoints, container queries and intrinsic layout, which supersede parts of the recipe. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: Mobile First
authority: Product designer (Yahoo chief design architect, co-founder of Polar), established expert on web forms and mobile design.
caveats: Usage statistics are dated; the case is strategic and design-oriented. For desktop-beside-simulator use mobile-first is a method, not a target. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: Le Modulor: essai sur une mesure harmonique a l'echelle humaine applicable universellement a l'architecture et a la mecanique
edition: English: The Modulor, Faber and Faber, 1954; Modulor 2, 1955
authority: Charles-Edouard Jeanneret (1887-1965), architect; the Modulor is the best known human-scale proportion system of the 20th century.
caveats: Based on golden-ratio and Fibonacci reasoning, which is aesthetic conviction not demonstrated perceptual advantage (Markowsky1992, Falbo2005). Used in a few buildings, never widely adopted. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: Reading Online Text: A Comparison of Four White Space Layouts
publisher: Software Usability Research Laboratory, Wichita State University
authority: Usability lab study from Wichita State University's Software Usability Research Laboratory, published in its Usability News newsletter and widely cited on margins and leading for screen text. Author list and order were not fully confirmed.
caveats: Small laboratory study with student participants, 2004 screens and text; effect of margins on speed and comprehension was modest; leading changed preference only. Not a replication-tested finding.

title: How nothing became something: White space, rhetoric, history, and meaning
authority: Peer-reviewed in the leading consumer research journal; tests and historicizes the meaning of white space.
caveats: About advertising, not learning or reading. Findings are cultural and historical: white space means what it does through its history, and the 2013 follow-up (Int. J. Research in Marketing, 30(3), 211-218) found cross-cultural differences.

title: Misconceptions about the golden ratio
authority: Computer scientist and mathematician at the University of Maine; the standard citation for debunking golden ratio claims.
caveats: Focused on mathematical and historical claims; psychological experiments on rectangle preference are treated briefly.

title: The golden ratio: a contrary viewpoint
authority: Mathematician at Sonoma State University; measured nautilus shells and re-examined claimed golden-ratio evidence in art, nature and psychology.
caveats: A critical review by one author; his own nautilus sample was modest in size.

title: The Power of the Center: A Study of Composition in the Visual Arts
authority: Rudolf Arnheim (1904-2007), Gestalt psychologist of art; author of Art and Visual Perception (1954).
caveats: Theoretical Gestalt analysis of artworks, little controlled experimentation. Claimed left-right asymmetries are mixed in later research. Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).

title: The Non-Designer's Design Book
authority: Best-selling practitioner and teacher; her four principles are the most widely taught layout heuristic for non-designers.
caveats: A teaching heuristic with no empirical validation of its own; sits on Gestalt research (lane 07). Bibliographic details recalled from memory; web verification was not possible (search budget exhausted, host blocked).
